question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-8 & -6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 6 \\ 1 & 6 & -4\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=PD{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that $A=PD{P}^{-1}$ is a diagonalization of the matrix $A.$ So let's apply the diagonalization algorithm to $A.$

**Step 1.** From the diagonal matrix $D,$ we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=-7\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=7.$

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$

- Consider $\lambda =-7.$ Then,

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 6 \\ 1 & 6 & -4\end{aligned}]-(-7)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -6 & -3 \\ 2 & 12 & 6 \\ 1 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -6 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 12 & 6 & 0 \\ 1 & 6 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -6 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are free variables. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-6{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-6{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

As a result, we have two linearly independent eigenvectors

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- Consider $\lambda =7.$ Then,

$$
\begin{aligned}A-7I & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & -6 & -3 \\ 2 & 5 & 6 \\ 1 & 6 & -4\end{aligned}]-7[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-15 & -6 & -3 \\ 2 & -2 & 6 \\ 1 & 6 & -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking for nonzero solutions of $(A-7I)x=0,$ we obtain the eigenvector 

$\,$ ${v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 3.** We construct the invertible matrix $P$ using our eigenvectors, as follows:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-6 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
